title: Current and Provision
premise: Xanthe Thackeray, a railroad engineer who keeps to the forgotten coastal branch lines of a monsoon-lashed peninsula, has spent years mapping routes nobody rides and answering to nobody at all. When an extreme low tide exposes a sea cave said to hold the lost payroll vault of a wrecked colonial railway, Xanthe's quiet survey work makes him the only witness—and the only person with the technical knowledge to reach it. A stranger named Wren Odile, claiming to be an archivist, forces her way into his expedition, and together they survive a flooding monsoon, a sabotaged trestle, and the slow revelation that Wren knows exactly who Xanthe used to be before he erased himself. Betrayed by the salvage syndicate that hired Wren and hunted by the flood itself, Xanthe must choose between the vault's truth—which names his own father as the saboteur of the wreck—and the found family he never intended to build. In the end he opens the vault, publishes the truth at the cost of his anonymity, and chooses to stay visible, riding the reopened line with Wren and the villagers who refused to let him drown alone.
about_author: A. M. Underhill is the pen name of a former track surveyor turned novelist who spent a decade documenting abandoned rail corridors across monsoon coastlines. Their fiction blends engineering precision with salt-weathered folklore, and 'Current and Provision' is their third adventure novel.

chapters.title: The Lines Nobody Rides
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. He surveys a derelict coastal branch alone, establishing his self-imposed invisibility, his meticulous map of closed lines, and the ritual that keeps the past at arm's length. Emotional beat: contentment built on avoidance, with a hairline crack of loneliness beneath it.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Back
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. An unprecedented low tide exposes a sea cave beneath the old cliff tunnel, its mouth framed by rusted rail iron and a carved marker matching a legend the villagers tell for tourist coin. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as he realizes the map he's made has led him here.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Signal Box
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Wren Odile arrives at his signal-box shelter claiming to research wreck records, too well-equipped and too curious about the cave. He lies about what he found; she clearly doesn't believe him. Emotional beat: wary chess, two people fluent in concealment recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Legend Charges Admission
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the village tavern she hears the full legend—the wrecked payroll train, the vault sealed in the cave, the men who drowned trying to reach it—and realizes Xanthe's survey notes match the wreck's true coordinates. Emotional beat: her hidden commission tightening; guilt she doesn't yet name.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Barometers drop, the harbor master orders boats hauled out, and the seasonal flood that isolates the peninsula each year begins its approach. Wren offers to fund an expedition to the cave before the window closes. Emotional beat: the ticking clock made physical; Xanthe's refusal and his own curiosity at war.

chapters.title: Terms of Passage
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. He agrees to take Wren by boat to the cave—his terms: she touches nothing without him, and she answers one question honestly at journey's end. They provision the leaking boat, patching it together with salvaged rail fittings. Emotional beat: grudging partnership, the first unforced laugh between them.

chapters.title: Down the Closed Line
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The boat run along the drowned track bed, navigating submerged culverts by his own maps, Wren proving unexpectedly capable. They reach the cave at slack water and enter by lamplight. Emotional beat: awe and competence in concert; trust beginning to form in the dark.

chapters.title: Iron and Bone
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Inside the cave: the wreck's forward carriage, fused to rock, and a sealed strongroom door stamped with a railway crest—and his father's inspector number. Xanthe goes silent; Wren notices. Emotional beat: the past reaching through stone to grab him by the collar.

chapters.title: The First Water
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The tide turns early and the cave begins to flood; they barely escape with photographs and a brass plate pried from the door. On the open water the monsoon's first bands hit. Emotional beat: adrenaline, then the cold arithmetic of a storm that will not stop.

chapters.title: Leaking Boat, Rising Sea
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Bailing and patchwork repairs through the night, engine flooding, the coast unreachable. They shelter in a flooded quarry cutting as the storm makes landfall. Emotional beat: raw survival stripping away pretense; Wren starts to tell the truth in fragments.

chapters.title: What Wren Knows
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Confession by firelight in the quarry: she works for the Corvane Salvage Syndicate, hired to locate the vault, and she was given Xanthe's name—because Corvane knows who he is, and what his father did. Emotional beat: betrayal offered honestly; Xanthe's world tilting.

chapters.title: The Name I Buried
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. He tells her his own history: the inspector's son who found his father's sabotage ledger as a boy, changed his name, and vanished into closed lines to keep the secret from surfacing. Emotional beat: two liars finally empty; the strange relief of being fully seen.

chapters.title: The Trestle Gives Way
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The flood undermines the quarry's rail trestle; they escape inland with Wren's injured shoulder and Xanthe's maps, reaching the half-abandoned village of Ferrymouth as it battens down. Emotional beat: the villagers take them in without questions—first taste of the found family.

chapters.title: Provision
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Days trapped in Ferrymouth by the flood: shared labor, a communal kitchen, a child who adopts Xanthe as her personal engineer, and the discovery that Corvane's advance team has arrived in the village asking after them. Emotional beat: warmth under siege; Wren realizing what she's been sent to take from these people.

chapters.title: Corvane Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Corvane's fixer, Halloway, makes Xanthe an offer: the vault's contents in exchange for erasing Wren's contract and leaving Xanthe's past buried. He refuses—but Halloway reveals the syndicate already has a second way into the cave, and it will collapse the cliff line. Emotional beat: coercion wearing a polite face; the stakes turn from treasure to catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Village Decides
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Xanthe lays everything before the villagers—his name, his father, the vault, the risk to the cliff their homes sit on. Instead of turning him out, they offer boats, hands, and the old tunnel plans kept in the chapel archive. Emotional beat: the found family choosing him back; loyalty as a decision, not a debt.

chapters.title: Race the Slack Water
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The storm's eye passes; a brief calm window. Xanthe, Wren, and three villagers race to the cave to shore up the cliff line and reach the vault before Corvane's demolition crew. Emotional beat: desperate momentum, every skill he ever buried now load-bearing.

chapters.title: The Strongroom Opens
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Using his father's number as the combination—truth as the only key—he opens the strongroom: the payroll is long gone, but inside is the full sabotage ledger, his father's confession, and proof the wreck was ordered by the railway's own directors, Corvane's founders among them. Emotional beat: grief and vindication tangled; the vault was never about money.

chapters.title: Collapse
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Corvane's crew detonates the cliff approach early; the cave floods as the team escapes with the ledger, one villager trapped behind the falling rock. Xanthe goes back for him against all sense. Emotional beat: the climax—courage against the wilderness that forgives nothing, and Wren choosing Xanthe's side over her contract.

chapters.title: After the Water
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The rescue succeeds barely; Halloway is caught by the flood he ordered, and Corvane's claim dies with the evidence now in the villagers' hands. Xanthe, half-drowned, wakes in Ferrymouth surrounded by the people who refused to let him be a stranger. Emotional beat: exhaustion transformed into belonging.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The ledger goes to the inquiry; Corvane's founders fall, the wreck's dead are formally acknowledged, and Xanthe's father's name is spoken in daylight at last. Wren tears up her contract and stays. Emotional beat: truth as the only loyalty that holds; the past finally set down instead of carried.

chapters.title: The Reopened Line
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Spring: the coastal branch is restored, and Xanthe drives the first train through the repaired cliff tunnel with Wren in the cab and the village waving from the platform. He signs his real name to the logbook for the first time in fifteen years. Emotional beat: resolution—visibility chosen, family found, the map of closed lines redrawn open.
